State 0 returns at once. State 7, with [[world+0x30]+0x10e0]+0xcf0 also 7, waits on [world+0x30]+0x1118 (0x143ac0100) when [world+0x30]+0xf58 >= 2 and sets that state to 0; any other state calls Ne_PhysWorld_AdvanceStepState(world) until world+0xcf0 is 0. Then, when byte rcx+0x69 is set, it calls Ne_PhysUpdateStage_FlushSubstepRecords(rcx) and tail-jumps to Ne_PhysWorld_NotifyBodyStepCallbacks(rcx). void: the caller reads no rax after the call (0x14445b283 loads r12). Correction to the earlier row: the list NotifyBodyStepCallbacks walks (world+0x40, next +0x40) holds constraints, not bodies. Ne_PhysWorld_CreateConstrainedBody builds those entries with +8 = body A (the +0x18 of the first handle), +0x10 = body B, +0x40 = 0 and the callback block at +0x80 (0x1440cdd47-0x1440cdda1, 0x1440cf017), and the values it hands the callback are the lengths of the entry's own +0x170/+0x180/+0x190/+0x1a0 vectors. The rigid bodies are on world+0x48, linked through body+0x330 (prev +0x338): Ne_PhysWorld_CreateRigidBody links each new body at the head (0x1440c06e9-0x1440c071b, world = [its rcx+8]), Ne_PhysWorld_RunStepPipeline steps its cursor world+0x50 through +0x330 and wraps it to world+0x48 (0x1440c77bd-0x1440c77da), Ne_PhysWorld_ResetFrameState walks the list (0x1440e07f8-0x1440e0847), and the body teardown 0x1441011a0 unlinks from it under the lock [[body+0x368]+0x60] (0x144101481-0x1441014d4). Body fields: +0x1c0 is row 3 of the world transform +0x190..+0x1cf, the position (Ne_PhysBody_SetTransform stores it at 0x1440c17fe); +0x220 is the linear velocity (Ne_PhysBody_ApplyImpulse adds J times the inverse mass +0x438 at 0x1440c1310-0x1440c1325 when flags +0x46c bit 0 is set; only the bit 1 path then clamps its length to +0x400 at 0x1440c13b8-0x1440c1414); +0x210 is the angular velocity (ApplyImpulse adds the inverse inertia rows +0xd0..+0x100 times (point - [+0x378]) x J at 0x1440c1335-0x1440c13b0 when bit 1 is set, then limits each axis to +0x3f4..+0x3fc in the frame +0x150..+0x170); +0x458 is the body's handle (0x1440c07b8), whose +0x18 is the body. Steam 26566308 0x1440ca340, EA 1.0.141 0x1440b62a0 and EA 1.0.145 0x1440b8870 have the same instruction stream (branch targets function-relative, RIP displacements masked), and so do NotifyBodyStepCallbacks, RunStepPipeline, AdvanceStepState, FlushSubstepRecords, RunSubsteps, ApplyImpulse, SetTransform, ResetFrameState, CreateRigidBody, CreateConstrainedBody, the teardown and Game_PhysicsUpdateStage_Update. callers: census steam 0x40c7d70. Core's physics non-finite log wraps it: after the game's code it walks world+0x48 once per update that finished a step and logs each body whose +0x1c0, +0x210 or +0x220 holds a value that is not finite once; it writes nothing to the game.
